topic: x86-64 Integer Arithmetic and Multiplication/Division Instructions
explanation: This concept describes how the x86-64 architecture handles integer arithmetic, specifically focusing on multiplication and division operations at the assembly level. Understanding these instructions is crucial for systems programming because they directly impact performance and efficient memory usage, especially when dealing with large integers that exceed the native word size of the processor.

extraction_metadata.source: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)

book: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)
code_example:
; Basic Integer Ops
ADD  RAX, RBX      ; RAX += RBX
AND  RCX, RDX      ; Bitwise AND
SHL  RSI, 4        ; Logical Shift Left

; Unsigned Multiplication (64x64 -> 128-bit result)
MOV  RAX, 0x100
MUL  RBX           ; RDX:RAX = RAX * RBX

; Signed Multiplication (3-operand variant)
IMUL RDX, RSI, 12  ; RDX = RSI * 12 (64-bit result)

; Division Setup (Sign extension of RAX)
CQO                ; RDX:RAX dividend preparation

; Unsigned Division (Uses RDX:RAX as dividend)
DIV  RSI           ; RAX = Quotient, RDX = Remainder

; Signed Division
IDIV RDI           ; RAX = Quotient, RDX = Remainder
keywords: x86 assembly multiplication, MUL IMUL DIV IDIV, x86-64 integer arithmetic
